items.name: Abi
items.source_text:
/// ABI definition (selector width/format).
pub trait Abi {
    type Selector
    /// Higher-kinded type constructor for a decoder over some `ByteInput`.
    type Decoder: * -> *
    /// ABI encoder type.
    type Encoder: AbiEncoder<Self>

    /// Size of the selector in bytes.
    const SELECTOR_SIZE: u256

    fn selector_from_prefix(_: u256) -> Self::Selector

    fn decode_bool_word(_: u256) -> bool
    fn decode_u8_word(_: u256) -> u8
    fn decode_u16_word(_: u256) -> u16
    fn decode_u32_word(_: u256) -> u32
    fn decode_u64_word(_: u256) -> u64
    fn decode_u128_word(_: u256) -> u128
    fn decode_i8_word(_: u256) -> i8
    fn decode_i16_word(_: u256) -> i16
    fn decode_i32_word(_: u256) -> i32
    fn decode_i64_word(_: u256) -> i64
    fn decode_i128_word(_: u256) -> i128
    fn decode_error() -> !

    fn decoder_new<I: ByteInput>(_: own I) -> Self::Decoder<I>
    fn decoder_with_base<I: ByteInput>(_: own I, _ base: u256) -> Self::Decoder<I>

    fn alloc(_ size: u256) -> u256
    fn encoder_new(_ size: u256) -> Self::Encoder
    fn encoder_at(_ base: u256) -> Self::Encoder {
        let mut e = Self::encoder_new(0)
        e.set_base(base)
        e.set_pos(base)
        e
    }
    fn store_word(ptr: u256, value: u256)
}

#[inline(always)]
pub fn decode_frame_from<A: Abi, T, I>(_ input: I, _ pos: u256, _ input_len: u256) -> T
    where T: Decode<A> + AbiSize,
          I: ByteInput,
          A::Decoder<I>: AbiDecoder<A>
{
    checked_frame_end<A>(pos, T::HEAD_SIZE, input_len)
    T::decode_from_prechecked_head(input, pos, input_len)
}

docs.body:
Effect reference traits.

 Fe models effects as implicit "provider" generic parameters. The `EffectRef<T>` marker traits
 express that a provider type can satisfy a read-only (or mutable) effect whose domain is `T`,
 while `EffectHandle` captures concrete pointer/handle providers with a runtime representation.

 Backends may define their own concrete provider types, but `core` also provides a small set of
 general-purpose provider types (`MemPtr<T>`, `StorPtr<T>`) that backends can map onto their
 runtime model.
 The address space an effect provider points into.

 Backends decide how each space maps onto their runtime model:
 - `Memory`: transient linear memory.
 - `Calldata`: an immutable input byte buffer (e.g. EVM CALLDATALOAD).
 - `Code`: immutable code data.
 - `Storage`: the target's persistent storage/state.
 - `TransientStorage`: a temporary store scoped to a call frame or
   transaction (e.g. EVM TLOAD/TSTORE).

Backends may define their own concrete provider types, but core also provides a small set of

 implementing type inside a contract field, the layout draws the slot
 number from `SPACE`'s slot counter instead of the containing field's, so
 statically assigned slots never collide with other state in that space.

items.name: Unknown
items.source_text:
/// A runtime bound value.
pub struct Unknown {}

docs.body:
A range from start to end (exclusive).

 The bounds can be either compile-time known (`Known<N>`) or runtime (`Unknown`).
 This allows for zero-cost ranges when bounds are known at compile time:
 - `Range<Known<0>, Known<10>>` - 0 words (fully const)
 - `Range<Known<0>, Unknown>` - 1 word (common `0..n` pattern)
 - `Range<Unknown, Unknown>` - 2 words (fully dynamic)
docs.html_body:
A range from start to end (exclusive).

The bounds can be either compile-time known (Known<N>) or runtime (Unknown).
This allows for zero-cost ranges when bounds are known at compile time:

  • Range<Known<0>, Known<10>> - 0 words (fully const)
  • Range<Known<0>, Unknown> - 1 word (common 0..n pattern)

string

docs.body:
Concatenates two fixed-size strings using their effective (unpadded) lengths.

 The result is left-padded with zeros to fill `OUT` bytes.

 If `a.len() + b.len() > OUT`, the result is truncated on the right (i.e. it
 keeps as much of `a` as possible, then as much of `b` as fits).

docs.body:
Maps a Fe type to its Solidity ABI type name.

 The compiler uses this trait to build event signatures at compile time.
 For example, `u256::SOL_TYPE` is `"uint256"` and `Address::SOL_TYPE` is
 `"address"`. The `#[event]` desugaring generates a `TOPIC0` constant
 from these values:

 ```
 const TOPIC0: u256 = keccak((Transfer::SOL_TYPE, "(", Address::SOL_TYPE, ",", u256::SOL_TYPE, ")"))
 ```

 Implement this trait for custom types to use them as event fields.

docs.body:
Solidity `bytesN` for `1 <= N <= 32`.

 The ABI representation is a single word with the `N` bytes left-aligned and
 the remaining bytes zero-padded. `val` stores the human-sized value
 right-aligned; e.g. `FixedBytes<4> { val: 0x01ffc9a7 }` encodes as
 `0x01ffc9a7...00`.

 Use the aliases `Bytes1` through `Bytes32` for Solidity-compatible source
 signatures. Encoding or decoding an unsupported width (`N == 0` or
 `N > 32`) reverts.

docs.body:
Allocate a `Bytes` of byte length `LEN` from `N` u256 words.

 `LEN <= N * 32`; slack in the last canonical word is preserved in memory but
 outside `LEN` is not part of the canonical value. Extra words beyond the
 canonical padded length are ignored. The function reverts with empty
 returndata when `LEN > N * 32`.

 This is useful for fixed-size byte sequences that are passed through
 Solidity ABI dynamic `bytes`, such as a 48-byte BLS public key backed by two
 words.

items.source_text:
fn is_canonical_ecrecover_signature(v: u256, r: u256, s: u256) -> bool {
    (v == 27 || v == 28)
        && r > 0
        && r < SECP256K1_ORDER
        && s > 0
        && s <= SECP256K1_HALF_ORDER
}

EC pairing check on a pre-built memory buffer (precompile 0x08).

 The buffer at `offset` must contain N pairs, each 192 bytes:
 `G1.x, G1.y, G2.x_imag, G2.x_real, G2.y_imag, G2.y_real`.
 Total length must be `N * 192`.

 Returns true if the pairing equation holds:
 `e(a1, b1) * e(a2, b2) * ... * e(aN, bN) == 1`

 Use effects (RawMem) to build the buffer, then pass it here.

reaches contract storage, the layout assigns the slot from the
contract's transient slot counter — shared with TStorPtr provider
fields, so static and runtime transient slots never collide.

docs.body:
A storage-backed value guarded by a transient reentrancy lock.

 The lock bit lives in transient storage at a slot assigned by the
 contract layout (through the zero-sized `lock` field), alongside runtime
 `TStorPtr` provider fields, so lock slots never collide with other
 transient state. The protected value is only reachable through
 [`Mutex::lock`] / [`Mutex::try_lock`] borrows; [`Mutex::peek`] offers an
 unguarded read for `Copy` values (e.g. read-only handlers), which does
 not protect against read-only reentrancy.

docs.body:
Hash two adjacent SSZ chunks as `sha256(left || right)`.

 This is the fundamental Merkle-tree primitive: an internal node is
 the SHA-256 of its two children's 32-byte digests. Most callers
 use the higher-level `Merkleize` trait; reach for `hash_pair`
 directly when building an incremental tree (the deposit contract's
 `branch[]` accumulator is the canonical example).

docs.body:
Pack a `uint64` SSZ basic value into a 32-byte chunk.

 SSZ basic integers are little-endian and right-padded with zeros
 inside the chunk. For `uint64` that means: 8 LE bytes occupy the
 **high** 8 bytes of the u256 word (offsets 0..8 of the memory
 chunk), the remaining 24 bytes are zero.

 Equivalent reference form (slower):
 ```ignore
 let mut chunk: u256 = 0
 for i in 0..8 { chunk |= ((value >> (i*8)) & 0xff) << (256 - (i+1)*8 ... )) }
 ```

 The implementation byte-swaps the low 64 bits with three SWAR-style
 passes (8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit), then shifts the result into the
 high 8 bytes of the chunk. The `#[arithmetic(unchecked)]` is
 required because the byte-swap relies on wrapping multiplication-
 free shifts that the bounds checker can't otherwise prove safe.

docs.body:
Serialize a `uint64` as a Solidity-compatible `bytes memory` value.

 Returns 8 little-endian bytes wrapped in the ABI `bytes` layout
 (length-prefixed, padded to a whole word). Used to emit `uint64`
 fields through a `bytes` log topic — e.g. the deposit contract's
 `amount` and `index` fields are serialized this way before being
 included in the `DepositEvent` payload.

 Note: the on-wire layout matches `u64_chunk` (LE in the top 8
 bytes of a word), wrapped with `len = 8` and `size = 64`.

docs.body:
Merkleize a tuple of pre-computed chunk roots into a single SSZ
 hash-tree-root.

 The tuple shape encodes the number of chunks in the value. For
 `N` chunks the trait pads to the next power of two (`P >= N`)
 with zero leaves on the right and computes the root of the
 balanced binary tree over `P` leaves.

 Implemented for tuple arities 1..=16, covering all SSZ containers
 in current consensus types (the wider beacon-chain containers like
 `BeaconBlockBody` decompose into sub-roots first, then merkleize
 at arity ≤16).

 Usage:
 ```ignore
 let root: u256 = (chunk0, chunk1, chunk2, chunk3).merkleize()
 ```

docs.body:
Mix the actual element count of an SSZ list into its Merkle root.

 SSZ distinguishes `Vector[T, N]` (fixed length, root = merkleize of
 chunks) from `List[T, N]` (variable length, root = `sha256(M || L)`
 where M is the merkleized chunks padded to the type's capacity N
 and L is the length as a `uint64` chunk).

 Call this on the merkleized capacity-padded root with the actual
 element count to get the canonical `List` root. The deposit
 contract uses it on `deposit_count` to finalize `get_deposit_root`.
docs.html_body:

docs.body:
A storage-backed packed array of fixed-bit-width integer lanes.

 Multiple lanes are packed into each 256-bit storage slot, and consecutive
 indices live in consecutive slots — so this is only meaningful for dense
 integer indices (token IDs, user IDs, order IDs, sequence positions).
 Passing addresses or hashes as `i` would spread one value per slot and
 is strictly worse than `StorageMap`.

 `BITS` must be a power of two that divides 256 — one of
 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. The constraint is enforced at compile time
 via `PackedBits<BITS>: ValidPackedBits`; invalid widths fail type-checking
 with a "trait bound is not satisfied" error.

 `SALT` is the layout seed. Lanes are stored starting at
 `keccak256(SALT)` (computed at compile time per monomorphization),
 so each array occupies a region of the 256-bit slot space that is
 effectively collision-free with any other field — adjacent inferred
 salts produce hashed bases ≈2²⁵⁶ apart. When the array is declared
 as a contract storage field, `SALT` is inferred automatically.
 Supply it explicitly only when you need a stable layout — for example
 with `core::keccak("myapp.storage.foo")` for upgradeable contracts.

 # Example

 ```fe
 // As a contract field — salts are inferred per-field:
 struct Store {
     order_status: StoragePackedArray<8>,
     order_tier:   StoragePackedArray<4>,
 }

 // With an explicit namespaced salt:
 const ORDERS_NS: u256 = keccak("myapp.storage.order_status")
 fn write_order_status() uses (storage: mut RawStorage) {
     let mut order_status: StoragePackedArray<8, ORDERS_NS> = StoragePackedArray::new()
     order_status.set(42, 1)
 }
 ```

 and L is the length as a `uint64` chunk).

 Call this on the merkleized capacity-padded root with the actual
 element count to get the canonical `List` root.

items.name: StoragePackedArraySeal
items.summary:
A storage-backed packed array of fixed-bit-width integer lanes.

 Multiple lanes are packed into each 256-bit storage slot, and consecutive
 indices live in consecutive slots — so this is only meaningful for dense
 integer indices (token IDs, user IDs, order IDs, sequence positions).
 Passing addresses or hashes as `i` would spread one value per slot and
 is strictly worse than `StorageMap`.

 `BITS` must be a power of two that divides 256 — one of
 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128.

items.name: ValidPackedBits
items.summary:

 — power of two ≤ 128, so 256 divides evenly into `256 / BITS` lanes.

pub enum AddressSpace
```

 Effect reference traits.

 Fe models effects as implicit "provider" generic parameters. The `EffectRef<T>` marker traits
 express that a provider type can satisfy a read-only (or mutable) effect whose domain is `T`,
 while `EffectHandle` captures concrete pointer/handle providers with a runtime representation.

 Backends may define their own concrete provider types, but `core` also provides a small set of
 general-purpose provider types (`MemPtr<T>`, `StorPtr<T>`) that backends can map onto their
 runtime model.
 The address space an effect provider points into.

 Backends decide how each space maps onto their runtime model:
 - `Memory`: transient linear memory.
 - `Calldata`: an immutable input byte buffer (e.g. EVM CALLDATALOAD).
 - `Code`: immutable code data.
 - `Storage`: the target's persistent storage/state.
 - `TransientStorage`: a temporary store scoped to a call frame or
   transaction (e.g. EVM TLOAD/TSTORE).

uses (mem: mut RawMem)
```

 Allocate a `Bytes` of byte length `LEN` from `N` u256 words.

 `LEN <= N * 32`; slack in the last canonical word is preserved in memory but
 outside `LEN` is not part of the canonical value. Extra words beyond the
 canonical padded length are ignored. The function reverts with empty
 returndata when `LEN > N * 32`.

 This is useful for fixed-size byte sequences that are passed through
 Solidity ABI dynamic `bytes`, such as a 48-byte BLS public key backed by two
 words.

pub struct FixedBytes<const N: usize>
```

 Solidity `bytesN` for `1 <= N <= 32`.

 The ABI representation is a single word with the `N` bytes left-aligned and
 the remaining bytes zero-padded. `val` stores the human-sized value
 right-aligned; e.g. `FixedBytes<4> { val: 0x01ffc9a7 }` encodes as
 `0x01ffc9a7...00`.

 Use the aliases `Bytes1` through `Bytes32` for Solidity-compatible source
 signatures. Encoding or decoding an unsupported width (`N == 0` or
 `N > 32`) reverts.

 Maps a Fe type to its Solidity ABI type name.

 The compiler uses this trait to build event signatures at compile time.

pub fn mix_in_length(root: u256, len: u64) -> u256 uses (mem: mut RawMem)
```

 Mix the actual element count of an SSZ list into its Merkle root.

 SSZ distinguishes `Vector[T, N]` (fixed length, root = merkleize of
 chunks) from `List[T, N]` (variable length, root = `sha256(M || L)`
 where M is the merkleized chunks padded to the type's capacity N
 and L is the length as a `uint64` chunk).

```fe
pub fn u64_chunk(_ value: u64) -> u256
```

 Pack a `uint64` SSZ basic value into a 32-byte chunk.

 SSZ basic integers are little-endian and right-padded with zeros
 inside the chunk. For `uint64` that means: 8 LE bytes occupy the
 **high** 8 bytes of the u256 word (offsets 0..8 of the memory
 chunk), the remaining 24 bytes are zero.

 Equivalent reference form (slower):
 ```ignore
 let mut chunk: u256 = 0
 for i in 0..8 { chunk |= ((value >> (i*8)) & 0xff) << (256 - (i+1)*8 ... )) }
 ```

 The implementation byte-swaps the low 64 bits with three SWAR-style
 passes (8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit), then shifts the result into the
 high 8 bytes of the chunk. The `#[arithmetic(unchecked)]` is
 required because the byte-swap relies on wrapping multiplication-
 free shifts that the bounds checker can't otherwise prove safe.

docs:
```fe
struct StoragePackedArraySeal
```

 A storage-backed packed array of fixed-bit-width integer lanes.

 Multiple lanes are packed into each 256-bit storage slot, and consecutive
 indices live in consecutive slots — so this is only meaningful for dense
 integer indices (token IDs, user IDs, order IDs, sequence positions).
 Passing addresses or hashes as `i` would spread one value per slot and
 is strictly worse than `StorageMap`.

 `BITS` must be a power of two that divides 256 — one of
 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. The constraint is enforced at compile time
 via `PackedBits<BITS>: ValidPackedBits`; invalid widths fail type-checking
 with a "trait bound is not satisfied" error.

 `SALT` is the layout seed. Lanes are stored starting at
 `keccak256(SALT)` (computed at compile time per monomorphization),
 so each array occupies a region of the 256-bit slot space that is
 effectively collision-free with any other field — adjacent inferred
 salts produce hashed bases ≈2²⁵⁶ apart. When the array is declared
 as a contract storage field, `SALT` is inferred automatically.
 Supply it explicitly only when you need a stable layout — for example
 with `core::keccak("myapp.storage.foo")` for upgradeable contracts.

 # Example

 ```fe
 // As a contract field — salts are inferred per-field:
 struct Store {
     order_status: StoragePackedArray<8>,
     order_tier:   StoragePackedArray<4>,
 }

 // With an explicit namespaced salt:
 const ORDERS_NS: u256 = keccak("myapp.storage.order_status")
 fn write_order_status() uses (storage: mut RawStorage) {
     let mut order_status: StoragePackedArray<8, ORDERS_NS> = StoragePackedArray::new()
     order_status.set(42, 1)
 }
 ```
